summary: A city rent rule lets rents rise about as fast as prices, so a retiree whose Social Security rose less pays more each year for less left over.
realLife: Los Angeles covers about three quarters of its apartments with a yearly cap set by a price formula, plus extra for utilities a landlord pays. Authors of a tenant-side report proposed a different measure; housing staff recommended dropping the utility add-on and calculated a 2 percent cap under the alternative. The council had not voted before the next February rise, so the older formula held. One senior said her benefit was rising 2.5 percent while her rent was scheduled to rise 5 percent. Another tenant's rent was projected to rise about $135 a month after the February step. Landlords said labor, materials and insurance costs justify higher rises.
